ai.title: Meet Cloudflare Clef-omni: A 30B-A3B Multimodal Decision Model for Audio, Video, Image and Text
ai.brief: Cloudflare has released Clef-omni , a new open-weight member of its Clef decision model family. Clef-omni is a Cloudflare decision model that scores text, images, audio and video in 1 call. It arrived on October 9, 2026, 8 days after the original Clef and Clef-flash launch . The same update cut Clef-flash pricing below TypeSafe’s Jev and made hosted Clef roughly 2x faster. For developers, this removes the transcription and captioning steps that multimodal agent pipelines usually need. 3 Bottom line: Best: one call decides across 4 modalities. Worst: weaker accuracy than text-focused Clef on hard reasoning. What is a decision model? A decision model returns typed answers with probabilities instead of generated text. You send a state and a schema of questions. The model returns a probability for every allowed option. Clef supports 3 question types : noul (true or false), choice and score .

sec.title: Bitdefender finds preinstalled Android malware you can’t uninstall, seen in 150 countries
sec.brief: S. S. Offers $10 Million Reward for Alleged HAFNIUM Hacker Zhang Yu Bitdefender researchers discovered a campaign called Midnight Mimosa involving preinstalled Android malware on low-cost phones from different brands that use MediaTek platforms. The malware is built into the device firmware and may be hidden in different system packages depending on the model. It is already on the phone before the owner turns it on for the first time and cannot be removed. The malware has system-level privileges, allowing it to install and remove apps, grant permissions and download code from a remote server without the user’s knowledge. This gives its operators control over the infected devices and allows them to use them for different purposes, including building a large botnet. The campaign appears to be mainly financially motivated.
